Tu t’en es sorti. Pour cette année.

note: French (France), «tu», French typography with a non-breaking space before : ; ! ? and inside « » (as \u00a0 in fr.ts). To double-check: (1) «la lampe» for la luce everywhere (HUD «Lampe», «lampe à fond», «éteins la lampe», «Archie vient pour la lampe»); «lumière» would be more natural in a few radio lines but less consistent. (2) «Journal» for il Diario, so the clippings are «Coupure de presse» (not «coupure de journal»); «Carnet» was the alternative. (3) «Nuit bonus» / «Bonus» for the extra night and the Extra menu («nuit extra» reads as «great night» in French). (4) Hatch's count ends with «Prêt, pas prêt, j’arrive !», the usual French hide-and-seek call; the counting sheet in Hatch's den is described as «PRÊT PAS PRÊT». (5) The fish puns and some real names (FAO/DORIS names: Anoli de mer, Joël, Allache, Palomine, Mostelle de roche, Marbré (morme), Poisson-guitare commun; genus-level where unsure: Poisson-lanterne, Poisson-scie, Lagocéphale, Grenadier). (6) Volantino: speech bubble split «Nos / petits ont / faim !» like the Italian «I nostri / piccoli hanno / fame!»; «Débutants bienvenus !» for «Nessuna esperienza!»; «au crépuscule» used in both the invitation and the tear-off tabs (au coucher du soleil is too long for a tab). (7) Pastelli: written without the space before ! (a 6-9-year-old's hand, and it keeps the text short); JOYEUX ANNIVERSAIRE (19 letters, shrinks to fit; BON ANNIVERSAIRE would be shorter); MON TRÉSOR is Robin's (no gender mark needed). (8) den_lampy follows the Italian Journal text («3,1 KG – juillet 2003») although docs/LOCALIZZAZIONE.md says the drawn card now reads «3100 g – 7 / 2003». (9) Keys stay as in the source (W A S D, Q/E, Esc): the game reads e.key, so on French AZERTY keyboards W/A and Q/E are not where a French player expects them (ZQSD is the French convention).
